phases.name: Core product & macOS
phases.desc: SRS engine, entitlement, specialty-pack architecture complete. The macOS app is signed, notarized, and now publicly released — v0.1.0-beta.2 is a live, downloadable pre-release (macOS + Linux AppImage builds, working auto-update manifest). This closed a real gap found this week: the build had been notarized and ready since July 29 but sitting undistributed.

phases.name: Full curriculum, A1–B2
phases.desc: 126 units, 30,609 cards. Every level has shipped at target density and passed at least one adversarial content-quality audit.

phases.name: Windows & Linux desktop
phases.desc: OS-event hooks and packaging are code-complete on both platforms. A real Windows compile issue was found and fixed this week, confirmed via an actual Windows CI run (not just local reasoning). Still blocked on Windows code-signing setup and on real-hardware verification — see Blockers.

phases.name: Cloud sync, auth & push notifications
phases.desc: Done and live-verified end to end, now including real push delivery — not just the desktop app. A real account holder signed in via Apple through the actual desktop build, recorded reviews on two independent devices at once, and both were confirmed as separate entries in the production database with correct automatic conflict handling — no review ever silently overwritten or lost, by design. A visible last-synced status indicator ships in Settings so a user can tell at a glance whether sync is working. The push notification server — the last infrastructure piece before mobile could ship — is now fully provisioned in production (real Apple credentials, scheduled dispatch job) and live-verified on a real iPhone: server → Apple's push service → locked-phone banner → tap → a real review session, confirmed working end to end. A follow-on redesign also made interrupt scheduling coordinate correctly across a user's multiple devices (so a Pro subscriber with a phone and a laptop doesn't get double-interrupted), closed and audited across three formal review rounds plus sixteen further hardening rounds targeting a subtle multi-device edge case in how a signed-out or reinstalled device's registration is cleaned up — two small, real gaps that survived that hardening were found and closed the same day they were found, both already live in production.

phases.name: Mobile — iOS & Android
phases.desc: iOS is built and live-verified end to end on a real iPhone via TestFlight: a push notification (or a tap on a cold-started deep link) correctly opens a real review session, with sign-in, sync, and licensing all working together on-device. The only remaining step for iOS is App Store submission itself (export-compliance paperwork, screenshots, review) — not further engineering. Android has not been started; it shares the same underlying engineering (the push server, the mobile app shell) so its remaining scope is narrower than iOS's was, but its own platform-specific work — notification delivery via Google's push service, Play Store packaging — is still ahead of it. Both ship from the same codebase via Tauri's mobile target, not a separate native rewrite.

phaseMethodology: the 93% headline weights each phase by its share of remaining engineering scope to a full five-platform, synced release (Core 35% · Content 25% · Windows/Linux 15% · Sync 15% · Mobile 10%), not by how many tickets are closed. A raw ticket count would read materially higher and overstate where things stand.

content.note: Every level has shipped its full unit plan and cleared this project's mechanical quality gate (no unit missing a tier, no duplicate sentences, hints present). B1 sits furthest from its stretch card-count target — the tradeoff made there was breadth of grammar coverage over raw card volume; it does not affect the level's completeness or its audit status below.

blockers.title: Windows code-signing setup
blockers.desc: Release pipeline and signing code are written. Needs an Azure Trusted Signing account, identity verification, and six credentials supplied once, then Windows builds sign automatically going forward.

blockers.title: Windows / Linux hardware verification
blockers.desc: OS-level wake, unlock, and idle-detection hooks are written and compile clean, but have only been checked on macOS. Needs real Windows and Linux machines (or CI runners) for final manual verification.

blockers.title: iOS App Store submission
blockers.desc: The app itself is done and live-verified on a real device via TestFlight. What remains is Apple's submission process — export-compliance paperwork, store screenshots, and review — an owner/business step, not further engineering.
